analysis.summary: A PHP 5.6 web application with a custom MVC framework and MySQL 5.6, running on one CentOS 6 VM with Apache and a local Postfix relay. Deployments are manual over FTP and there is no redundancy, so every VM issue is an outage. The capability itself - field force call reporting - is a commodity CRM function.

tech_debt: Home-grown MVC framework with no documentation and no remaining author
No automated tests; deployments are manual FTP copies to production
App server, database and mail relay share one VM with no failover
Duplicate HCP master records across regions
Monthly CSV export instead of an integration
analysis.regulated_data: No GxP or patient data. Healthcare professional (HCP) names and contact details are personal data under India's DPDP Act.

dimensions.rationale: Language, database and OS are all years past end of support.
A single undocumented monolith; nothing is separately deployable.
evidence: App, DB and mail on one VM

dimensions.rationale: One VM with PHP sessions on local disk; no horizontal scaling or redundancy.
40 GB of MySQL with a simple schema migrates easily to a managed database or SaaS objects.
Only a monthly CSV export and outbound email.
Not GxP; the main obligation is DPDP-compliant handling of HCP personal data.
evidence: HCP contact details are personal data (DPDP Act)

dimensions.rationale: Manual FTP deployments, no tests, no monitoring.

risks.title: Exploitable PHP 5.6 vulnerabilities
risks.description: An internet-facing PHP 5.6 app on CentOS 6 receives no security patches.
risks.mitigation: Put a WAF in front immediately and fast-track the migration; restrict admin pages by IP.

risks.title: Low adoption by field reps
risks.description: Reps may resist a new tool mid-quarter, hurting call-reporting compliance.
risks.mitigation: Pilot with one region, involve rep champions, provide offline mobile app and short video training.

risks.title: Duplicate and dirty HCP master data
risks.description: Duplicate HCP records would carry into the new system and distort call metrics.
risks.mitigation: Deduplicate and standardise HCP records before migration; assign a data steward.

risks.title: DPDP consent and notice gaps
risks.description: HCP personal data may lack recorded consent or purpose notices required by the DPDP Act.
risks.mitigation: Host in an India region, capture consent in the new platform and document processing purposes.

risks.title: SaaS licence cost overrun
risks.description: Per-user SaaS pricing for 640 users may exceed the limited budget.
risks.mitigation: Negotiate tiered pricing; compare against a low-code replatform option before signing.

risks.title: Custom features lost in the move
risks.description: Sample-drop tracking quirks may not map one-to-one to SaaS objects.
risks.mitigation: Run a fit-gap workshop; configure custom objects only for the gaps that matter.

risks.title: Reporting gap during cutover
risks.description: Managers may lose weekly reports for a cycle during switchover.
risks.mitigation: Cut over at week start and run both systems in read-only parallel for one cycle.

opportunities.title: Mobile-first with offline mode
opportunities.benefit: Reps log calls in the field even on poor networks.

opportunities.title: Real-time manager dashboards
opportunities.benefit: Weekly CSV reports become live dashboards.

opportunities.benefit: No VM patching, backups or outages to manage.

opportunities.title: Daily warehouse feed
opportunities.benefit: Sales analytics move from monthly to daily data.

plan.headline: Repurchase: replace RepConnect with a life-sciences SaaS CRM in about 15 weeks, piloting one region first and retiring the end-of-life VM.

patterns.name: SaaS replacement
patterns.why: Field force call reporting is a commodity CRM capability; custom code adds no differentiation.

patterns.name: Event-driven integration
patterns.why: A managed SaaS-to-cloud data flow replaces the fragile monthly CSV export.

component_strategies.rationale: A life-sciences SaaS CRM (e.g. Veeva CRM or Salesforce Life Sciences Cloud) provides call reporting, visit planning, sample tracking and an offline mobile app.
Data migrates into SaaS objects; a read-only archive is kept for history.
A managed SaaS connector delivers daily data to the warehouse.
SaaS CRM notifications and dashboards replace emailed reports.
Decommission the CentOS 6 VM after cutover and archive.
Corporate warehouse stays; it receives a daily feed instead of a monthly file.
